paper_title: WebGLM Towards An Efficient Web-Enhanced Question Answering System with   Human Preferences
caption: retriever time analysis.
model_annotation: This stacked bar chart illustrates a retriever time analysis across different statistical metrics. The horizontal axis displays the categories, which are labeled sequentially as "Avg.", "50%", "75%", and "90%". The vertical axis represents the time value, labeled "sec." for seconds, and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to approximately 9.5, with numerical tick labels placed at regular intervals of 2.0. Each category features a single vertical bar composed of four stacked segments, visually separated from one another by thin white outlines. As indicated by the legend in the upper left, the segments represent different system processes, arranged from bottom to top as follows: "Search" (dark blue), "Fetch" (medium blue), "Extract" (light blue), and "Retrieval" (very light blue). The total heights of the bars vary, with the "50%" category forming the shortest total bar at approximately 3.7 seconds, and the "90%" category forming the tallest at approximately 9.2 seconds. The intermediate "Avg." and "75%" bars reach total heights of roughly 5.3 and 5.4 seconds, respectively. Within the stacks, the bottom "Search" segment ranges from approximately 1.3 seconds in the "50%" bar to 2.0 seconds in the "90%" bar. The "Fetch" segment represents the largest individual component in each stack, adding roughly 1.7 seconds to the "50%" bar and up to 5.0 seconds to the "90%" bar. The "Extract" segment is the thinnest across all categories, contributing roughly 0.2 to 0.4 seconds to each total, while the topmost "Retrieval" segment adds between 0.5 seconds in the "50%" stack and 1.8 seconds in the "90%" stack. The categories are ordered by statistical percentile rather than being sorted by magnitude, and no individual bars are visually emphasized.
